_comment_canonical: DUNE FD-HD 1x2x6 TrackFitting configuration (wcp-porting-validation wcfm/docs/25), consumed by TaggerCheckNeutrino through the 'trackfitting_config_file' knob of pgrapher/experiment/dune10kt-1x2x6/pr.jsonnet; the path is resolved through WIRECELL_PATH. Keys starting with '_' are skipped by load_trackfitting_config. Values are WCT internal units (mm, us; cm^2/s = 1e-7; ms = 1e6). Read at RUNTIME: a byte-identical compiled jsonnet does NOT mean the fit is unchanged.
_comment: Forked BY DUPLICATION from sbnd/sbnd_track_fitting.json (untouched): the FD PR job runs SBND's neutrino operating point, so every selection / fit knob is SBND's value (incl. the doc sbnd_xin/118 lattice pair and the doc 119 proj pad). Differences: the six detector keys (DL, DT, add_sigma_L, ind_sigma_u_T, ind_sigma_v_T, col_sigma_w_T) and the electron-lifetime pair (electron_lifetime, electron_lifetime_allow_unmatched).
_comment_diffusion: DL = 7.2 cm^2/s, DT = 12.0 cm^2/s: the values the FD WCT simulation drifts with (dune10kt-1x2x6/simparams.jsonnet inherits pgrapher/common/params.jsonnet lar.DL/DT; wcfm/docs/07). The fit must use the sample's own diffusion (the SBND lesson, sbnd_xin/docs/66). Not the physical 0.5 kV/cm coefficients -- change both together if the simulation changes.
_comment_longitudinal: add_sigma_L = 1/(2*pi*Gaus_wide 0.12 MHz) * drift 1.6 mm/us = 1.32629 us * 1.6 = 2.1221 mm (dune10kt-1x2x6/sp-filters.jsonnet Gaus_wide 0.12 MHz; clus_params.jsonnet drift_speed 1.6 mm/us, the speed the grouping is configured with).
_comment_transverse_smearing: SEED VALUES, NOT MEASURED ON FD. ind_sigma_u_T / ind_sigma_v_T / col_sigma_w_T are PDHD's EMPIRICAL widths (pdhd_track_fitting.json, doc pdvd/42-44): FD has the same APA wires (4.67/4.67/4.79 mm pitch, 35.7 deg) and the same induction wire filter (Wire_ind 0.75/sqrt(pi)); its collection filter is wider (Wire_col 3.0/sqrt(pi) vs PDHD 10.0/sqrt(pi)), so col_sigma_w_T is likely underestimated. Re-derive with pdhd/docs/scripts/d44_sigma_fit.py on an FD arm; never from the SP filter closed form.
_comment_lifetime: electron_lifetime 8 ms (8e6 internal) is the FD simulation's lar.lifetime (pgrapher/common/params.jsonnet), which the Drifter applies and SP/imaging do not undo (2.27 ms full drift => 25 % charge loss at the cathode). It only acts on clusters with a matched flash, i.e. on NONE here (no light). electron_lifetime_allow_unmatched (C++ default 0) would extend it to these clusters, but it is 0 HERE ON PURPOSE: on FD event 1311 the on/off fitted-dQ ratio was NOT the per-point factor exp(t/tau) -- a uniform +14 % offset and a slope 1/1461 cm instead of 1/1280 cm, mechanism not identified (wcfm/docs/25 sec 5.3). Uncorrected attenuation is the known bias; set it to 1 only once that is understood.
_comment_skip_revert_iso_xext_cut: doc pr/28 sec 17 round 10 (toolkit 6b219d14). C++ default -1 (off, unconditional revert). 200.0 = 20 cm (units::cm=10) -- SBND production default since 2026-08-06 (owner: 'overall better, please turn it on for these for SBND', gate work-pr28r10-flip vs -on48b single-event byte-identical; population gate work-pr28r10-on48b vs -off48b already on record, doc pr/28 sec 17.4 G4/G5). Abstains from skip_trajectory_point's charge-consistency revert when the point's cluster has blob-center drift-x extent below this cut -- i.e. isochronous clusters only; non-isochronous clusters (including doc pr/28 sec 13's evt 388) are unconditionally unaffected.
_comment_d118_fit_lattice_knobs: doc sbnd_xin/118, FLIPPED for SBND on the owner's go 2026-09-20. The two doc pdvd/101 track-fit lattice knobs, the same pair PDHD and PDVD production carry (pdhd_track_fitting.json doc pdvd/108, pdvd_track_fitting.json doc pdvd/103). fit_weight_pow 1.5 replaces the fit's q^2 point weight by q^1.5; assoc_cont_center 1 centres the association window on the cell instead of rounding it. C++ defaults are 2.0 and 0, so REMOVING these two keys restores the pre-flip fit exactly. Flipped as ONE PACKAGE with the trajectory knobs in clus.jsonnet (retile 'charge_stepped'; Steiner 'prefer3' / 0.5 / 'tree+path' at both passes): doc 116 sec 16.3 measures the vertex gain as super-additive and LARGEST with these two keys -- nuecc within 1 cm 599 -> 640 of 1626 without them (+2.5 pt, p 0.027) and 669 with them (+4.31 pt, -145/+215, p 0.00027); median nearest-candidate distance 0.960 -> 0.840 cm (p 0.00026); the SELECTED signal's own vertex 0.850 -> 0.780 cm on nuecc>4 (p 0.00026) and 0.830 -> 0.760 cm on cv numu (p 0.017). No primary metric of doc 107's package is degraded (M1-M8 all 'not separable', doc 116 secs 5 and 9). THIS OVERRIDES A FROZEN RULE: doc 116 sec 15.4 recommended against the flip and doc 117 sec 11's ADOPT table returned HOLD, because that round pre-registered the vertex-distance metric as SECONDARY; the owner overrode it explicitly on the trajectory closure plus the vertex accuracy. What is still unconfirmed: the 1 cm gain is one sample at p 0.0003 and one (cv) at p 0.078, and cv is not separable at 3-5 cm -- doc 117 sec 10.2's independent-sample replication remains the open item. KNOWN COSTS carried by this flip, measured in doc 116 sec 14: +10 % of the PR-stage compute on cv and +19 % on nuecc against a same-conditions control (all of the CPU is the retile knob, these two keys are free); the nu_e peak-RSS tail 1.52 -> 2.21 GiB with 5 events of 2001 above 2 GiB, so a 2 GiB per-process cap no longer holds on nu_e-like events (2.5 GiB does, cv is unchanged at 1.37 GiB); 10-13 % of the selected signal changes identity, so the uBooNE BDT operating points and doc 107's cut package are now tuned against a different trajectory; and med_d_W 0.2381 -> 0.2459 wires is the one closure clause these two keys move the wrong way. MUST stay paired with dl_vtx_dual_chain=true: doc 117 sec 5.2 grades the trajectory with fit_exclusion=false as the worst cell of its grid (M8 -1.17 pt, p 0.016). Read at RUNTIME by TaggerCheckSTM and TaggerCheckNeutrino: a byte-identical compiled jsonnet does NOT mean the fit is unchanged.
_comment_d119_proj_pad: doc sbnd_xin/119 round 2, FLIPPED for SBND on the owner's go 2026-09-21. Same values PDHD and PDVD have carried since doc 30 round 3: restricts the fitted 2-D charge DISPLAY product to cells within 3 wires and 3 time SLICES of a cell the fit actually predicts (the seed is the raw R*pos_3D prediction, not pred_charge, so a dead channel crossed by the track is not dropped). C++ default -1 = OFF; REMOVING these two keys restores the pre-flip display exactly. WHY THIS WAS FLIPPED, AND WHY THE REASON IS NOT THE ONE IN doc 30: on PDHD this knob bought -28.8 % core-s and -56 % peak RSS because PDHD stored ~362 k cells per call and kept only 2.4 % of them. SBND IS NOT IN THAT REGIME. Doc 119 sec 6 measured it on the 62-event gate manifest: SBND keeps 87.9 % of its proj cells, its map holds 7 968 cells per event (PDHD's, WITH the knob already on, holds 9 153 -- SBND without it was already tighter than PDHD with it), peak RSS moves -0.1 % mean and -0.3 % worst-event, and the apparent +2 % CPU is INSIDE the null-pair noise floor (ctl vs ctl2: +0.2 / -1.6 / -2.6 %). So this flip buys NO CPU and NO MEMORY on SBND, and doc 119 recommended against it. The owner flipped it anyway on 2026-09-21 for CROSS-DETECTOR CONSISTENCY: all three detectors now run the same trajectory family (doc pdvd/103, doc pdvd/108, doc sbnd_xin/118) and SBND was the only one whose 2-D display settings differed. DO NOT quote a CPU or memory saving for SBND from this key -- there is none. WHAT IT CHANGES: T_proj_data and the calib dump's proj block, i.e. the 2-D scan display, and nothing else. It is a real loss of 12.1 % of the display cells (7 968 -> 7 002 per event), not a free change. GATED on 62 events (doc 119 sec 6, docs/119_figs/119_gate_pad.txt): T_rec_charge, every tagger tree, mabc-pr.zip, the pctree, nusel and the non-proj calib dump are ALL identical; only T_proj_data, the proj block and the fit-JSON provenance move. The same gate on a null pair (one configuration run twice) returns 10/24/1 where this returns 28/48/21, so it is sensitive as well as specific. Every reader of the trimmed map is a dump writer -- PrDisplayDump.cxx:1173 states the blast radius is diagnostic-only; no tagger verdict, Bee layer or pctree tensor depends on it. Read at RUNTIME by TaggerCheckSTM and TaggerCheckNeutrino: a byte-identical compiled jsonnet does NOT mean the display is unchanged. uBooNE and the two ProtoDUNEs are unaffected -- TrackFitting.cxx is shared, and each detector's own *_track_fitting.json selects the behaviour.
